newsitem.title: USA: IBM prices new OS/2 Warp at $249 and $149.
newsitem.headline: IBM prices new OS/2 Warp at $249 and $149.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. has priced the newest version of its OS/2 Warp operating system at $249 for first time OS/2 users and $149 for those upgrading from previous versions, an executive said Tuesday.
OS/2 Warp version 4 will feature built in voice recognition technology, and built-in support for the Java application development language for Internet applications.
It also bundles in Netscape Communications Corp.'s Navigator browser for Internet use.

"We think that is a pretty incredible price when you consider Netscape Navigator is in there as well as voice recognition. Voice recognition is typically a $700 add on," John Howard, worldwide brand manager for OS/2 Warp, said in an interview.

IBM has struggled to increase its 9 percent market share in the desktop operating system market, a struggle which puts it against Microsoft Corp.'s approximately 80 percent market share with Windows and makes it neck and neck for second place with Apple Computer Inc.'s Macintosh operating system.
OS/2 Warp, because it is popular in the corporate desktop market, is positioned mostly against Microsoft's Windows NT operating system for corporate desktop networks.
